nodes.title: Candidate prompt shapes for the judge's BLIND-10 false positives (all at 0.85: hunger, EMI and boss hyperbole; rat poison stored at home), NOT applied to judge.json. (a) Add to 'crisis is false for': 'complaints that something (a bill, an EMI, a boss, hunger, heat) is killing or finishing them, said about the thing rather than a wish to die'. (b) Add: 'poison, pesticide or medicine that is kept, bought or used for its ordinary purpose (rats, crops, a prescription)'. (c) Keep 'if unsure, prefer crisis true' but tie it to self-reference: 'only when the words could be about harming themselves'. Needs a new PREREG, DEV runs for both labels and a fresh blind set (BLIND 11 is ready). Prompt length must stay at or below A's, since B and C showed length costs timeouts.
nodes.closes_when: A PREREG'd prompt change passes on DEV and a blind set, or the shapes are rejected.

nodes.title: The judge's real recall loss is timeouts (both BLIND-10 misses; DEV unavailable 4-10%). The runtime judge never blocks the reply, so a longer budget (for example 1,800 ms) only moves more verdicts from 'acts on this reply' to 'acts from her next sentence or turn'. Measurement path, now in the runtime: VP_SAFETY_JUDGE_TIMEOUT_MS (clamped 500-3000) overrides judge.json timeout_ms without editing the contract, and every reply logs 'verdict in/not yet at her first sentence (budget N ms)' (Conversation.judge_in_time). On staging, run the same calls at 1,500 and 1,800 ms and compare unavailable (judge events) against verdicts not yet in at the first sentence; then decide judge.json timeout_ms.
nodes.closes_when: Staging numbers at both budgets and a decision on timeout_ms.
